stem: What is the group of individuals or the system that makes rules and ensures they are followed called?
explanation: Correct option: (B). The chapter calls the group or system that makes rules and makes sure they are followed a government. A community is simply people living together, a committee is a small group for a task, and a market is a place for buying and selling.

stem: Students ask their school to change the timing of the lunch break, and the school agrees after discussion. What idea about rules in society does this best show?
options: Rules are made once and can never be changed
People affected by rules can have a say in them
Only students should decide the rules of a school
Rules matter only when there is a punishment
explanation: Correct option: (B). The chapter says rules and laws are not set once and for all; just as students may ask a school to change a rule, citizens also have a say in the laws governing society. The rule here did change, so it was not fixed forever; the school still took part, so students did not decide alone; and nothing in the case involves punishment.

stem: Read the case 'Catching the online thieves'. The cyber police tracing and arresting the criminals is an example of which organ of government at work?

stem: What is the main purpose of keeping the three organs of government separate?
options: To let each organ check the others
To stop the organs from ever meeting
To give all power to the legislature
To remove the need for any courts
explanation: Correct option: (A). Separation of powers provides checks and balances: each organ can check what the others do and restore balance if one acts beyond its role. The organs still interact and work together, no single organ gets all power, and courts remain essential.

stem: Suppose the same small group of people made the laws, enforced them and also judged every case. What is the most likely result?
options: Laws would be fairer because fewer people decide
The group could misuse power with nobody to check it
Courts would become faster and always more just
Citizens would gain more say in making the laws
explanation: Correct option: (B). If all three organs were under one group, no organ could check another, so power could easily be misused; this is exactly what separation of powers prevents. Fewer decision-makers does not make laws fairer, speed does not guarantee justice, and citizens would have less, not more, say.

stem: What are the three levels at which government functions in India?

stem: Why does India follow representative democracy rather than having every citizen vote on each law?
options: Most citizens are not allowed to vote at all
Representatives are chosen by the courts
Laws in India need no discussion or debate
Hundreds of millions cannot all decide together
explanation: Correct option: (D). With about 970 million voters in 2024, it is not practical for all citizens to decide every matter, just as a whole class cannot go to the principal, so people elect representatives. All citizens above 18 can in principle vote, representatives are elected by people not courts, and laws are discussed and debated in assemblies.

stem: Which situation is the best example of grassroots democracy?
options: Ordinary villagers have a say in deciding where a well is dug
A national court gives its final ruling on an appeal
The Prime Minister meets leaders of other countries
A Governor gives a speech at a State function
explanation: Correct option: (A). Grassroots democracy enables ordinary citizens, the base of the pyramid, to have a say in decisions that affect them; villagers deciding on a local well fits this.
